world 1 (key leveled).reader_note: Sand dropped in hollows plus straight furrows and even wheat yields 'leveled'; 'nourished' is killed by wheat no thicker in the hollows, 'irrigated' literally describes the flooding.

world 2 (key marooned).reader_note: New channel with no crossing until 1963 between villages and fields decides marooned; fresh silt lures nourished, but fields unsown eleven years kill it and irrigated.

world 3 (key nourished).reader_note: Dark mud followed by record harvests in ordinary-rain years gives nourished; winter wheat 'withered as badly as on the dry terraces' kills irrigated (a literal fit for a flood) and water soaking away within weeks kills marooned.

world 0 (key irrigated).reader_note: After three dry years the wheat came up thick on flooded farms but withered on the terraces, so the gain was water; 'ran clear' kills nourished (no silt), boundaries left as they were kills leveled, and marooned has no support.

world 2 (key isolated).reader_note: The exclusive-contract sentence decides it alone; 'designed from scratch' kills mimicked and 'judged equal' kills leapfrogged.

world 3 (key infiltrated).reader_note: Paid draftsmen still on the rival's payroll plus models arriving weeks before the rival's matching ones point to infiltrated; mimicked is the near-miss since the designs were copied, but via insiders and ahead of the rival.

world 0 (key mimicked).reader_note: 'matched the older company's model part for part, down to the shape of the keys' alone hands over mimicked, reinforced by buying and dismantling it; 'same dealers' makes infiltrated a literal near-fit and outselling lures leapfrogged, but part-for-part copying kills a leap.

world 1 (key leapfrogged).reader_note: An electric machine the rival had dismissed, sharing not one part, then outselling it, decides leapfrogged; mimicked is killed by sharing no parts, and selling through the same dealers weakens isolated and infiltrated.

world 0 (key milked).reader_note: Equal duck predation kills manipulated and equal bacterial death kills immunized; smaller size, fewer eggs and an unchanged lifespan favor 'milked', but neutered is defensible from the reduced eggs, though they still lay a third.

world 1 (key immunized).reader_note: Bacterium killing nine in ten uninfected but one in ten infected decides immunized; equal duck predation kills the classic manipulated, and 'slightly' fewer eggs and slower growth kill neutered and milked.

world 2 (key manipulated).reader_note: One planted phrase per distractor: 'laid as many eggs' kills neutered, 'grew as large ... lived as long' kills milked, the bacterium 'killed both kinds alike' kills immunized; climbing to where ducks feed gives manipulated.

world 3 (key neutered).reader_note: 'Laid no eggs at all' decides neutered; ducks taking both kinds at the same rate kills manipulated, the bacterium killing both alike kills immunized, and milked is weak.

world 0 (key inn).reader_note: One day's stop in burrows then moving on, never trapped twice, gives inn; lair is killed by 'never twice', lane by the east-west hedge crossing a north-bound route, larder baited by voles.

world 1 (key lair).reader_note: Females denning in the bank spring to late summer with young born there decides lair; 'hunted in the oak woods' kills larder and 'crossing the open fields' kills lane, inn fails on season-long residence.

world 2 (key lane).reader_note: 'came out of its western end within an hour' kills lair, inn and larder in one phrase; voles burrowing in the bank make larder a literal lure, but east-to-west dispersal through the hedge gives lane.

world 3 (key larder).reader_note: Nightly winter hunting, burrows emptied by late winter, and stoats staying away in summer when the woods have voles decide larder; lair is killed by stoats going back to their woods before dawn, and lane by each returning to the wood it came from; inn is the weak member.

world 1 (key metronome).reader_note: Uniform layers 'whatever the weather' and others dating cores against its count point to a timekeeper, metronome; ledger (exact count of years) is close. Shared shrimp and plankton lure microcosm.

world 3 (key museum).reader_note: Relict species 'vanished from every other lake' make it unrepresentative (kills microcosm) and a window on the ice-age past (museum); the yearly layers lure ledger/metronome until 'churned its layers past reading'.

world 0 (key ledger).reader_note: Yearly layers giving the only rainfall record points to ledger, but 'the shrimp and plankton in its water are those of every lake nearby' plus 'studied more closely than any other lake' arguably supports microcosm (a typical lake studied as a sample of the region). If that sentence is meant to kill microcosm it does the opposite; the author should rewrite it.

world 2 (key lookout).reader_note: Mortuary fails on a surface read (no burials). The wall facing the ford, spear tips and crossing-week hearths give lookout; the riverside camp with bedding and children kills lodge; the freezing back chamber is the icebox lure.

world 3 (key mortuary).reader_note: Walled layers of uncut human bones with an antler laid on each decide mortuary; the ledge over the ford lures lookout and the cold chamber lures icebox, while camps by the river kill lodge.

world 0 (key icebox).reader_note: Near-freezing chamber, unburned stacked joints, and autumn cuts eaten in late winter combine to cold storage; hearths and children's teeth 'in a camp by the river' kill lodge; the cliff overlooking the ford makes lookout a literal fit.

world 1 (key lodge).reader_note: The back chamber 'stays near freezing' literally fits icebox and the ford view literally fits lookout, but winter hearths after the herds left, bedding, hide scrapers and children's shed milk teeth together point to a dwelling; mortuary is killed because milk teeth are shed, not left by the dead.

world 3 (key mortgaged).reader_note: Bank lump sum, half-yearly repayments, deed back after the last payment: mortgaged. The deed returning kills liquidated, the oak woods lure logged.

world 0 (key leased).reader_note: Wages replaced by fixed yearly sums from forty households decides leased; the 1858 inventory with oak woods intact kills logged and liquidated, money coming in rather than out kills mortgaged.

world 1 (key liquidated).reader_note: Three buyer-type sums exceeding thirty years' profit plus 'no wages, rents or repairs' then only share dividends point to a sale; 'no ... rents' kills leased, and the timber merchant makes logged a literal near-fit that the landowner and auctioneer undercut.

world 2 (key logged).reader_note: A naval shipyard payment from an oak-wood estate, then extra men hired to pull stumps and sow grass, means timber was sold; the regular hands' wages running on to 1858 kill liquidated and leased, and nothing marks the payment as a loan (mortgaged). The reader has to infer the timber.

world 0 (key insurance).reader_note: The five-year gap matching the famine reads as savings drawn on in hard times, so insurance; local coins and local-style jewelry kill loot, kitty is the near-miss (a pooled fund).
